2. Heard Sri Suneel Kumar Mishra, learned counsel for the applicants, Sri Surendra Kumar Jaiswal,
learned counsel for the opposite party no.2, Sri Bade Lal Bind, learned counsel for the State and perused the records.

3. The present application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed by the applicants-Hasan Mohammad, Najar Mohammad, Smt. Fatima Nisha, Abdul Gaffar, Smt. Guddu Nisha and Sareer Mohammad with the prayer to allow the present application and quash the entire proceeding as well Hasan Mohammad And 5 Others vs State Of U.P. during the pendency of present application.
4.

sentences.text: The matter was referred to the Mediation Centre of this Court vide order dated 22.5.2024 for making an effort between the parties for settling their disputes amicably.
The dispute between the parties is matrimonial in nature.
5. As per the office report dated 6.2.2025, a report from the Mediation Centre of this Court is on record.

6. As per report of Mediation Centre dated 26.09.2024, the parties have amicably settled their dispute and further decided to live separately and further agreed to withdraw the cases going on between them.

7. Learned counsel for the applicants has produced a demand draft of Rs.100000/- (One Lakh only)
in favour of opposite party no.2/wife, the photocopy of the same has been produced before the Court which is taken on record, the same is being handed over to learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 in compliance of Clause 7(d) of settlement agreement dated 26.9.2024 entered into between the parties before the mediation and conciliation centre of this Court.
8. Learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 accepts the same.
He shall be endorsing the receipt of the same on the order sheet of the present matter today.
He submits that he has no objection to the same.

9. The law with regards to quashing of a case on the basis of settlement arrived between the parties,
is well settled.

The Apex Court in the cases of (1) B.S. Joshi and others Vs. State of Haryana and another: (2003)4 SCC 675; (2) Nikhil Merchant Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation : (2008) 9 SCC 677; (3) Manoj Sharma Vs. State and others: ( 2008) 16 SCC 1; (4) Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab:
(2012) 10 SCC 303; (5) Shaifullah and others Vs. State of U.P. And another: 2013 (83) ACC 278 and (6) Parbatbhai Ahir@Parbatbhai @ Bhimsinbhai Karmur and others Vs. State of Gujarat and another: (2017) 9 SCC 641 has held that the cases in which the parties have settled their grievances can be quashed.
